name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
DO: Auto-apply formatting-only patches to our own prompt files.

Formatting-only patches are low-risk, high-reward. They enforce consistency without changing meaning, making prompts easier to review and maintain. The trade-off is speed vs. safety—we skip human review for these trivial changes, trusting our linter to catch real errors. This frees us to focus on higher-impact improvements.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t formatting drift—it’s that a misapplied patch could silently corrupt a prompt’s logic if the formatter misinterprets whitespace as semantic (e.g., YAML indentation breaking a conditional). A better alternative is to auto-apply *only* to files with a `.fmt` suffix, gated by a pre-commit hook that rejects any change altering the prompt’s meaning. Settle it by running a diff against a held-out set of prompts to confirm no semantic drift occurs.
